segment.description: The short Tennessee reach of the North Fork Holston River in Sullivan County: from where the fork enters Tennessee from Virginia to its confluence with the South Fork Holston at Kingsport (the head of the Holston River main stem).
segment.boundaries: State line (the fork forms the TN/VA line for its final miles) downstream to the South Fork Holston confluence at Kingsport, per the catalog. The Virginia reach upstream (famous smallmouth/musky fishery, e.g. near Gate City VA) is OUT of scope and none of its facts transfer to this record.

coldSource.notes: No cold-water source identified or claimed: this is a free-flowing Valley-and-Ridge river reach with no dam upstream in Tennessee (nearest upstream station USGS-03490000 is in Virginia). USGS-03490090 'NORTH FORK HOLSTON RIVER NEAR CLOUD FORD, TN' (HUC 06010101, 716.91 sq mi drainage) and TDECWPC-NFHOL004.6SU (river mile 4.6, Carter Valley Rd bridge - i.e. inside this reach) verify the reach identity. SourcesChecked note: USGS identity endpoint 503 all week, so station identity was verified via WQP Station metadata CSV (bBox around Kingsport).

holdover.detail: Moot - no trout are stocked or documented in the Tennessee reach, so there is no trout population to hold over.

wildPopulation.detail: No trout presence of any kind documented for the TN reach. TWRA manages it through a black-bass special regulation (Smallmouth 13-17 in protected length range, one over 17 in/day, state line downstream to the South Fork Holston confluence), i.e. a warmwater black-bass fishery. The renowned smallmouth/musky river in VIRGINIA upstream is a different water and management regime.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Summer grab samples in the Sullivan County reach ran 22.7-29.5 C across 1995-2008 (USGS 03490090 and TDEC NFHOL004.6), and TWRA has no trout program on the river - zero stocking workbook rows and no appearance anywhere in the state trout regulations.
